title: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian regular schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-regular-scheme]. On each component suppose the codimension is $c\geq0$ and the ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $c$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. On ordinary small-etale derived categories with Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], the Kummer-supported fundamental-class morphism of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism:
$$\eta_{i,n}:\Lambda_{n,Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}(c)[2c].$$
Equivalently, $i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}$ has its sole cohomology sheaf in degree $2c$, canonically $\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)$. Here $i_n^!$ is the right adjoint of ordinary etale $Ri_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. No excellence, field-of-definition, or smoothness-over-a-field hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorem 3.1.1, applied to Noetherian regular pairs and the class of Definition 2.3.1; no excellence assumption in that theorem.

proof.text: Work first with $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $S$ be any complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait with $\ell$ invertible and let $V$ be integral regular, flat and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$. Apply [lem-per-trait-prime-to-ell-log-alteration] to obtain $f:Y\to V$ and a finite trait extension $T\to S$ with $Y$ integral regular, quasi-projective of finite type over both bases, log smooth over $T$, and $f$ projective dominant generically finite etale of degree $d$ prime to $\ell$. The finite-type Noetherian criterion makes $Y$ and $V$ Noetherian, since $S,T$ are spectra of Noetherian discrete valuation rings. Log-smooth punctual purity makes $Y$ punctually pure. Projective implies proper, so proper invertible-degree descent applies to $f$ over $S$, with both source and target integral regular and quasi-projective of finite type over that same complete trait. Since $d$ is prime to $\ell$, it is invertible in $A$. It follows that $V$ is punctually pure; no flatness of $f$ has been used.

source.place: XVI 3.7, printed pp.254--255; Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7

proof.text: Step 1 verifies the premise of the mixed-characteristic trait test for every such $S,V$, with the fixed prime $\ell$. Apply [lem-per-punctual-purity-trait-test]: every regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible is punctually pure for $A$. In particular both $X$ and $Z$ in the item are punctually pure. The test imposes no excellence hypothesis on these schemes.

Apply the punctual two-of-three statement to $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$: conditions (b) and (c) hold by Step 2, hence condition (a) holds. Thus the actual Kummer-supported morphism $\eta_{i,1}:A_Z\to i_1^!A_X(c)[2c]$ is an isomorphism. This is the class named in the item, not an unspecified isomorphism. The statement is local for the locally constant codimension, so it applies componentwise.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244; application in 3.7

proof.text: For the fixed pair, choose cones $C_r$ of its actual prime-power Kummer maps using [lem-per-gysin-coefficient-cone-triangles]. Step 3 says $C_1=0$. Induct on $r\geq1$: the supplied distinguished triangle $C_r\to C_{r+1}\to C_1\to C_r[1]$ has zero outer objects if $C_r=0$. Its cohomology long exact sequence gives $H^q(C_{r+1})=0$ for every integer $q$; cohomology detects derived isomorphisms, so $C_{r+1}=0$. This proves $C_n=0$ for every $n\geq1$, and hence the specified $\eta_{i,n}$ is an isomorphism. The cone lemma supplies compatibility of actual coefficient classes, not merely a reduction of their abstract isomorphism types.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.3.2 and proof, printed p.245

proof.text: First commute $i_n^!$ with the twist. The closed immersion $i$ is proper ([lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]: closed immersions are proper) and of finite type, so the trivial compactification $(1_Z,i)$ gives $Ri_!=Ri_*$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] with right adjoint $i_n^!$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The finite Tate lines are locally free of rank one, their pullbacks are the Tate lines of $Z$ and their negative twists are their duals, with evaluation isomorphisms $L\otimes L^{-1}\cong\Lambda_n$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; so $-\otimes L$ is an autoequivalence with inverse $-\otimes L^{-1}$. For $L=\Lambda_{n,X}(c)$, $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_n)$ and every $M$ on $Z$, adjunction, this inverse and the proper projection formula [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] for $i$ give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(M,i_n^!(K\otimes L))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_*M,K\otimes L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_*M\otimes L^{-1},K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_*(M\otimes i^*L^{-1}),K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes i^*L^{-1},i_n^!K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,i_n^!K\otimes i^*L)$. By Yoneda, $i_n^!(\Lambda_{n,X}(c))\cong(i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X})\otimes\Lambda_{n,Z}(c)$. Now tensor the isomorphism of Step 4 with $\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)$ and shift by $[-2c]$; evaluation (on a local basis $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$) cancels the twist and gives $i_n^!\Lambda_{n,X}\simeq\Lambda_{n,Z}(-c)[-2c]$, with cohomology only in degree $2c$, since tensor by a locally free line is exact, as checked in local bases. The empty immersion has zero objects throughout; in codimension zero the class is the open-and-closed restriction identity by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus].

source.place: XVI Theorem 3.1.1 and Definition 2.3.1; untwisting the conclusion (twist commutation of i^! by the projection formula)
